subject: design-technology

moments.title: Nitinol discovered
moments.who: William Buehler, US Naval Ordnance Lab
moments.body: Buehler discovers a nickel-titanium alloy that returns to its programmed shape when heated.
moments.takeaway: Military research often originates civilian materials.

moments.title: Piezoelectric effect
moments.body: The Curie brothers demonstrate that crystals produce voltage under stress, a property now used in sensors.

moments.title: E-paper Kindle
moments.body: Electrophoretic 'E-Ink' displays bring smart materials into mass-market reading devices.

now.title: Smart materials now
now.body: Self-healing concrete, photochromic glass and shape-memory polymers are reaching commercial use.
now.open_questions: Which smart materials will become 'invisible' infrastructure of the next decade?

reflection: Materials that 'remember' or 'respond' make products that adapt to their users.
